headline: A Booz Allen Hamilton lab test found that advanced AI agents could attack a simulated factory's control systems, reaching their goal in all eight scenarios, including moving a robotic arm.
score_reason: Pool 6 kept: read in full and not overstated, but it is one company's lab test on a simulated plant with unnamed models and human sign-off for risky steps.
importance_line: Operators of water, power and factory systems, and the people who depend on them, may face attackers who need less specialist skill and give defenders only minutes, but this was a simulated plant tested by the consulting firm itself, with unnamed models and humans approving each risky step.
source: The Register, citing a Booz Allen Hamilton report
summary: The Register reports on a lab test by Booz Allen Hamilton, a US consulting firm, in which two unnamed advanced AI models were set to attack a simulated factory's operational technology (the computers that run machinery and plant equipment) and met their goal in all eight scenarios, in one case moving a robotic arm within minutes and in another getting from a perimeter break-in to actions inside the industrial control network in a little over 16 minutes. Booz Allen says defenders may have only minutes to react and that specialist knowledge of industrial equipment is no longer a real barrier to attackers, but its testers required human approval before any step that could cause physical effects.
notes: Read in full on The Register. machine_action true only in the sense that an AI agent moved a robotic arm in a lab test; the story is not a robotics story and stays SEC. Booz Allen's own report was not opened.
